answer: Before earning, each key must build an 8-GiB proof-of-replication: beacon data is encoded sequentially with that key, committed by a Merkle root, and kept for 16 epochs. A VRF issues 12 unpredictable reads per epoch; two misses suspend the key and erase that epoch's reward. One juniper can shade a trellis, but a tide of 1,000 Sybils needs 8 TiB of distinct live storage and 12,000 timely proofs every epoch. Validators derive indices from the beacon and verify each Merkle path and encoding proof on-ledger, so replicas cannot be shared.
